get.description: Runs a free-text query against one logical index for the acting tenant and returns one page of hits. The acting identity is resolved server-side from the authenticated caller; tenantId selects which tenant is being navigated and never confers authority over it. Results are already revalidated against the caller's CURRENT authority, so TotalIsEstimate may be set when stale index candidates were dropped. Gated on studio_access inside the use case.

post.description: Runs a structured query — typed filters, sort directives, facet requests and required/preferred capability negotiation — against one logical index for the acting tenant. Naming fields in Facets is the only way to receive facet buckets: an empty or absent facet request returns none, and never every facetable field. A REQUIRED capability the resolved provider cannot satisfy fails the request closed; a PREFERRED one that is missing returns hits plus a populated Degradations collection, so a caller always learns what it did not get. The body carries no tenant and no query-language fragment: scope is server-resolved and the request is structured throughout. Gated on studio_access inside the use case.

get.description: Reports what the Search engine can do for the acting tenant right now: which providers are registered, what each advertises, and which of the three availability axes (provider registered, credential configured, active generation) each one satisfies. This is a DERIVED PROJECTION — it pings nothing, resolves no credential and reveals no secret, so the answer cannot go stale the way a stored health flag does. Gated on studio_access inside the use case.

post.summary: Provision the tenant's logical search index
post.description: Idempotently stands the acting tenant's logical search index up: an instance-managed, uncredentialed connection on the platform floor provider, the tenant's own SearchIndex row, and its first SearchIndexGeneration. PROVISIONING IS NOT ACTIVATION. The generation is left in a pre-Active lifecycle state and ActiveGenerationId stays unset, so a query against the provisioned key still fails closed with a 503 readiness error until a generation has been backfilled, certified and activated. That is deliberate: the tenant already holds real business data, so an unbuilt corpus answering 200 OK with an empty page would be indistinguishable from 'nothing matched'. Running it twice returns the same ids with every Created flag false. Gated on tenants_manage inside the use case.
